description: Stop the sandbox-executor test suite from mutating live sandbox state. Proven root cause of the bean 0019 orphan-commit incident: apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_intent_creator.py calls the real intent_creator.main() while patching only subprocess.run, os.path.exists and os.makedirs. get_workspace_dir() and cleanup_repo_dir() are NOT patched, and inside the executor container sandbox detection is always active (HOLON_ROLE=executor, /.dockerenv, USER=holon), so get_workspace_dir() resolves to the live /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace and cleanup_repo_dir(..., raise_on_error=True) reaches _rmtree() and deletes the executor's own workspace, because ~/.holon-sandbox is whitelisted in ALLOWED_PARENTS. Reproduced deterministically: with HOLON_ROLE=executor and the repository copied to the sandbox workspace, running only the test_intent_creator module leaves the workspace WIPED while all ten other test modules leave it ALIVE. Afterwards git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails, executor.py takes its destructive re-initialisation fallback, and the pushed execution branch is an orphan root commit containing only the ledger files.
goal: Make the whole apps/sandbox-executor test suite hermetic so that running it can never touch a real workspace, real user home directory, or a real git remote. 1) In apps/sandbox-executor/tests, ensure every test that invokes a role entrypoint (intent_creator.main, planner.main, executor.main, and their integration variants) pins the workspace to a per-test fixture: set HOLON_REPO_DIR to a tempfile.mkdtemp/tempfile.TemporaryDirectory path and patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir where they are not already patched, so cleanup_repo_dir can never receive a path outside the fixture. Audit every module in apps/sandbox-executor/tests, not only test_intent_creator.py. 2) Assert the invariant instead of trusting it: in the tests that exercise cleanup behaviour, assert that _rmtree / _clear_dir_contents is only ever called with a path inside the fixture directory, and add a dedicated guard test that runs the entrypoint test modules with HOLON_ROLE=executor and HOLON_IN_SANDBOX=1 and asserts the sandbox workspace path still exists and still contains its marker file afterwards. 3) Remove any real network or remote side effects from the suite: no test may reach a real github.com origin or push; every git remote used by a test must be a local temporary repository or a mock. 4) Keep the existing intent-creator behaviour assertions intact (branch generation, slug sanitisation, target_branch handling, intents.jsonl ledger payload) so the fix is proven to preserve behaviour. 5) Add a short note to apps/sandbox-executor/docs or the tests directory explaining that role entrypoint tests must always pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture, so this hazard is not reintroduced. Keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor, follow the repository Python, typing, linting and test conventions. IMPORTANT SANDBOX SAFETY RAIL, required while the hazard still exists in the checked out tree: never run the full discovery suite (python3 -m unittest discover, or pytest over the whole tests directory) inside the executor workspace at /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, because until your hermeticity fix is in place that run deletes the workspace out from under the executor and fails this execution. Instead verify your work in a scratch copy: export HOLON_REPO_DIR=/tmp/holon-test-fixture, copy the repository to /tmp/holon-fixture, run only the specific test modules you changed from that copy with PYTHONPATH=apps/sandbox-executor/src python3 -m unittest tests.test_intent_creator (and the other modules you edited), and only run full discovery from the /tmp copy, never from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace. Also note the sandbox image has neither uv nor pytest, so use PYTHONPATH=apps/sandbox-executor/src python3 -m unittest from a copy. Work efficiently and finish well inside five minutes: read the minimum files needed, apply the edits, verify with targeted module runs, and do not debug the sandbox environment itself.

description: The sandbox executor's post-agent git recovery path in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py is destructive and history-destroying. After the coding agent finishes, executor.py probes the workspace with 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' (check=False). When that probe fails it logs 'Warning: git repository invalid or missing after agent execution. Re-initializing git repo...', then deletes the workspace .git directory with shutil.rmtree, runs 'git init', pins the branch with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<exec_branch>' and re-adds the origin remote. There is no fetch, update-ref or reset step, so the following 'git add' / 'git commit' produce an orphan root commit whose tree holds only executions/<execution_id>.md and holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl, and 'git push -u origin <exec_branch>' then publishes a branch sharing no history with plan_branch or main. Live proof from the bean 0019 incident: pushed execution commit 1561bd3 has no parents and a two-file tree; the whole codebase and all parent history vanished. Deleting .git outright also destroys an object database and refs that may still have been perfectly usable, and the executor pushes regardless of whether recovery produced a base commit or whether the agent execution even succeeded. The only test covering this path, apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py::test_main_git_recovery_on_corrupted_repo, asserts nothing about history: it merely asserts that some command starting with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD' was issued (line 342), which locks in the defective behaviour instead of preventing it. This is acceptance criteria 2 and 5 of Bean 0019; the hermetic-tests half (criterion 1) already landed on main.
goal: Make the executor's post-agent git recovery non-destructive and history-preserving, and replace the misleading test. 1) PROBE AND REPAIR BEFORE ANY REBUILD: factor the post-agent check into testable helpers (for example _probe_git_repo and _repair_git_repo) that classify why 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' failed and repair the benign causes so a healthy repository is never rebuilt. Handle at least: (a) 'detected dubious ownership' by retrying the probe with '-c safe.directory=<repo_dir>' and persisting that entry in the repository-local config rather than global; (b) a stale '.git/index.lock' or 'cannot lock ref ... locked' condition; (c) GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_INDEX_FILE / GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY variables leaked by the agent runner process environment, which must be stripped from the executor's own git invocations; (d) a missing or dangling HEAD symref. Only when the repository is still unusable after these repairs may the rebuild path run. 2) NON-DESTRUCTIVE: never delete a .git directory. When a rebuild is genuinely required, move the old directory aside with os.replace or shutil.move to a sibling backup path inside the workspace such as '.git-unusable-<utc-timestamp>' and, after the fresh 'git init', append that backup path to '.git/info/exclude' (never to the tracked .gitignore) so 'git add -A' can never stage it. Log the backup path. 3) RE-ATTACH THE BASE COMMIT BEFORE STAGING: after 'git init', add or repoint the origin remote to get_repo_url(), then 'git fetch --no-tags origin <plan_branch>' with a bounded retry count and timeout configurable through HOLON_GIT_FETCH_RETRIES (default 3), then resolve the fetched tip, create the execution branch ref at that tip with 'git update-ref refs/heads/<exec_branch> <tip>', point HEAD at it with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<exec_branch>', and run 'git reset <tip>' in mixed mode (never --hard, never checkout -f) so the index matches the base commit while every agent-authored working tree change survives. The subsequent 'git add' plus 'git commit' must then yield a commit whose first parent is the plan_branch tip. 4) VERIFY PARENTAGE BEFORE PUBLISHING, OTHERWISE REFUSE TO PUSH: after committing, verify the recovered base is an ancestor of HEAD (for example 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <base_tip> HEAD') and that the committed tree still contains repository files. If the base commit cannot be recovered, or HEAD is not a descendant of it, log an actionable error naming the cause, write the execution record, mark the ledger entry 'status: failure' with a summary naming the git recovery failure and the backup path, commit locally if possible, and skip the push entirely. A branch with no parent must never be pushed, whatever the execution status. 5) PRESERVE EXISTING BEHAVIOUR for a healthy repository: the add, commit, push and HOLON_SKIP_PUSH handling of the normal path stays as it is, and the execution record and ledger payloads keep their current shape apart from the new failure status and summary. 6) TESTS: delete the 'git symbolic-ref HEAD' assertion from apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py::test_main_git_recovery_on_corrupted_repo and add real git regression coverage using temporary local repositories and local bare remotes only, never a network remote. Assert at minimum: after a corrupted or removed .git the resulting execution commit lists the plan tip as its parent and its tree still contains the codebase files together with executions/<execution_id>.md and holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl and the agent-authored edit; no rmtree of .git occurs on the recovery path; for the benign probe failures of requirement 1 (dubious ownership, stale index.lock, leaked GIT_DIR) the executor repairs and keeps using the existing repository without re-initialising; and when origin does not contain the plan branch the executor performs no push and records 'status: failure'. Every new or touched test must obey apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture directory, patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir, no real remote or network access, and the suite must pass for both the 'not integration_test and not stress' selection and the 'integration_test' selection. 7) CONVENTIONS AND VERIFICATION: keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor; follow the repository Python, typing and ruff conventions; run 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"' plus the integration selection; run 'npx prettier --write "**/*.md"' if any markdown changes; do not hand-edit the append-only ledger files in holon-knowledge/ledger. Honour the sandbox safety rail in apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: never run discovery from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, verify from an isolated copy under /tmp instead. Work efficiently and finish well inside the sandbox time budget: read only the files you need, apply the edits, verify with the targeted pytest selections, and do not debug the sandbox environment itself.

description: Two defects that were confirmed in the same bean 0019 sandbox run, both still unfixed on main. (1) Silently blind agent failures: apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py invokes the coding agent through run_cmd(agent_cmd, cwd=repo_dir, check=False) and then throws the captured output away. The execution record gets only 'Plan execution failed with exit code N' and the ledger entry gets the same one-line summary, so a failed run is undiagnosable after the container is gone. Live proof: execution E-1790379447-antigravity-agent-gemini-3.8-flash-medium recorded 'status: failure / Plan execution failed with exit code 1' while the real cause, visible only in the antigravity session database afterwards, was 'printmode.go:521] Print mode: timed out after 1488 polls'. Nothing in the committed execution record explained the failure. (2) A default remote that no longer exists: get_repo_url() in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/agent_runner.py returns https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder-ref.git when a token is present and git@github.com:Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder-ref.git otherwise. That reference repository was retired by Bean 0022 and no longer exists, so every flow run that does not export HOLON_REPO_URL clones and pushes a dead repository; harness runs only work today because HOLON_REPO_URL is exported by hand, which silently hides the defect.
goal: Two independent, small, well-tested changes. 1) RETAIN BOUNDED AGENT OUTPUT: capture the coding agent stdout and stderr in executor.py and persist them with the execution record so a failure is diagnosable from the branch alone. Add a bounded '## Agent Output' section to the executions/<execution_id>.md record containing the redacted tail of the agent's combined output, hard-capped at a configurable byte budget (HOLON_AGENT_LOG_BYTES, default 65536) with an explicit truncation marker stating how many bytes were dropped, and honour the existing HOLON_SKIP_PUSH behaviour. Redaction is mandatory: run the captured text through the existing redact_text() helper in executor.py and additionally strip the literal values of GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HOLON_AGENT_KEY if they appear, because the agent inherits those variables; no secret may reach a committed file. Never break the run for logging: every capture, truncate and write step must be wrapped so a failure only warns and the execution record is still written. Keep the existing record fields and ledger payload keys unchanged, adding only optional keys (for example agent_output_truncated and agent_output_bytes) so existing ledger readers keep working. 2) FIX THE DEFAULT REMOTE: change get_repo_url() in agent_runner.py so that the token-HTTPS branch and the SSH branch both target the active Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder repository, with HOLON_REPO_URL still taking absolute precedence, and grep apps/sandbox-executor for any remaining hard-coded holon-agentic-coder-ref reference (source, prompts, docs, tests, fixtures) and remove it, leaving the retired name out of shipped code. Do not change the token-prefix detection rules or the environment variable names. 3) TESTS: add hermetic unit tests that assert (a) a failing agent run writes an execution record whose Agent Output section contains the agent's diagnostic line and stays within the byte budget, with the truncation marker present when the cap is exceeded; (b) a token value taken from GITHUB_TOKEN or HOLON_AGENT_KEY never appears in the committed record or ledger entry; (c) a logging failure inside the capture path does not change exec_status or raise out of executor.main(); (d) get_repo_url() returns the holon-agentic-coder SSH URL when HOLON_REPO_URL and tokens are unset, the holon-agentic-coder HTTPS x-access-token URL when a gh-prefixed token is set, and returns HOLON_REPO_URL unchanged when it is set regardless of token; and (e) a guard test asserting no file under apps/sandbox-executor/src mentions holon-agentic-coder-ref. Every new or touched test must obey apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture, patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir where a role entrypoint is invoked, use no network and no real remote. 4) CONVENTIONS AND VERIFICATION: keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor; follow the repository Python, typing and ruff conventions; run 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"' plus the integration selection; run 'npx prettier --write "**/*.md"' if any markdown changes; do not hand-edit the append-only ledger files in holon-knowledge/ledger. Honour the sandbox safety rail in apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: never run discovery from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, verify from an isolated copy under /tmp instead. description: Every Holon flow PR currently fails the hygiene CI job on 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"' because intent, plan, execution, and calibration artifacts generated and committed by the flow roles and entrypoints are not formatted with prettier before commit. Furthermore, measured evidence from Bean 0019 (PR #61) shows that prettier formatting on planner-emitted markdown is not idempotent in a single pass: in PR #61, a first 'prettier --write' pass moved 303 lines but 'prettier --check' immediately failed again; a second pass moved 8 more lines before finally passing. This oscillation is charged against PR reviews rather than the generator, causing red CI runs, wasted review iterations, and fragile review resolver fixes.
goal: Implement automated prettier convergence across all flow-produced markdown artifacts and prompts: 1) CREATE CONVERGENCE UTILITY: Add a robust formatting helper (e.g. sandbox_executor.formatting.converge_prettier) that runs 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --write <files>' in a bounded loop (up to 3 passes) until 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check <files>' succeeds with exit code 0. If npx/prettier is unavailable or fails after max passes, fail loudly or log clearly without corrupting files. 2) INTEGRATE ACROSS ENTRYPOINTS: Invoke the convergence formatter before committing in: (a) planner.py for plans/P-*.md, (b) executor.py for executions/E-*.md and any modified markdown files, (c) calibration.py for calibration reports, and (d) flow.py across plan, execute, and calibrate pipeline stages so no flow branch is committed or pushed with failing markdown hygiene. 3) HARDEN PROMPT GUIDANCE: Update holon-config prompts/templates to advise agents against using raw unescaped underscores in arithmetic/metric formulas (e.g. recommend backticks or '*' for multiplication) so generated markdown is closer to a single-pass fixed point. 4) TESTS: Add hermetic unit tests verifying that the convergence helper converges oscillating markdown, succeeds on clean markdown, respects pass limits, and integrates with the entrypoints and flow runner. All tests must follow apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md. 5) VERIFICATION: Verify with 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .', 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"', and 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"'.

description: Beans 0054, 0060, 0065, and 0066 identify systemic defects in the Stage 5 post-execution calibration engine (sandbox_executor/calibration.py): 1) Bean 0054: 'holon calibrate' cannot survive execution branch deletion or resolution when the branch exists only on the remote (e.g. refs/remotes/origin/*), as a commit SHA, or as a PR head ref. Merging a flow PR consumes the execution branch, or calibrating in a fresh worktree where the branch has not been checked out locally fails with 'fatal: <branch> is not a commit'. 2) Bean 0060: 'holon calibrate' resolves branch names against stale local refs without fetching or checking the remote, and in parse_actual_metrics non-zero git diff exits are silently swallowed into '0 files modified', producing distorted SSA, entropy error, and EV calculations. Furthermore, executions.jsonl and executions/<id>.md are read from the host working tree instead of the execution git ref, and 'checkout -B' destructively overwrites already published /calibrated branches rather than fast-forward appending. 3) Bean 0065: The calibration report carried on the execution branch (plans/P-*_calibration.md) records an evaluation timestamp but no head commit SHA. When subsequent review commits land on the PR branch, the carried report becomes silently stale, flattering the run with outdated patch size and entropy metrics. Staleness must be mechanically detectable by recording the evaluated commit SHA and verifying it against the branch head. 4) Bean 0066: 'holon calibrate --no-commit' announces that it committed and created the calibrated branch even though nothing was committed and no branch was created or reset. The report and messages must accurately distinguish committed vs uncommitted runs, and include committed: false in --json output.
goal: Implement calibration integrity, resilience, and staleness detection across sandbox_executor/calibration.py, cli.py, and flow.py: 1) ROBUST REF RESOLUTION & FETCH (Beans 0054, 0060): In run_calibrate and generate_calibration, resolve execution and plan refs against remote refs (origin/<branch>), commit SHAs, or PR head refs (refs/pull/<n>/head or gh pr view --json headRefOid) if local refs are missing or stale. Fetch target refs before calculating metrics if running against remote tracking references. Do not require the execution branch to be checked out as a local branch. 2) LOUD FAILURES & PROVENANCE EXTRACTION (Bean 0060): In parse_actual_metrics, fail loudly if git diff --shortstat fails with non-zero exit; never treat an unresolvable ref as '0 files modified'. Read executions.jsonl and execution markdown records via 'git show <exec_ref>:<path>' (falling back to local file if ref unavailable) to ensure metrics reflect the execution commit rather than the host checkout's active branch. Assert the head SHA measured and warn if it differs from the PR head. 3) APPEND-ONLY CALIBRATED BRANCHES (Bean 0060): Make re-running stage 5 append-only: if <branch>/calibrated already exists locally or remotely, update the report as a fast-forward commit on top of it instead of destructively wiping it with checkout -B. 4) EVALUATED COMMIT SHA & STALENESS DETECTION (Bean 0065): In CalibrationReport, format_markdown_report, and JSON output, record the exact evaluated commit SHA ('- **Evaluated Commit SHA:** `<sha>`'). Implement staleness verification to check whether the evaluated commit SHA matches the current branch head, providing a helper/method to detect if a carried report is stale. 5) ACCURATE --NO-COMMIT LOGGING & JSON OUTPUT (Bean 0066): When --no-commit is specified, output clear messages indicating the report was written to the working tree and that no branch was created or committed. Omit the 'Calibrated branch: ...' announcement when no branch was created or reset. In --json output, include 'committed': false (or true) and 'evaluated_commit_sha'. 6) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Hermetic unit tests in tests/test_calibration.py covering: remote ref resolution, SHA targets, deleted branch fallback, non-zero diff failure, git show provenance reading, fast-forward /calibrated branch updates, evaluated commit SHA recording, staleness detection, and --no-commit messaging/JSON schema. Verify with 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .', 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"', and 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"'.

description:
redact_text in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py masks a credential only when it can see the credential's key name, and the accepted key names are a closed alternation (token, access_token, secret, password, api_key, auth, bearer, _pat, _key, -key, secret_key, private_key, signing_key, encryption_key, ...). A secret printed under any other name is committed verbatim to the execution record and ledger row. Key gaps identified in Bean 0062 include: 1) Common key names outside the list like bare 'key = ...', 'pwd = ...', 'client_secret', 'db_password', 'credential', and service SDK names are left unmasked. 2) The URL-query rule's anchor is [?&](token|api_key|...)[^=]*=, where [^=]* matches newlines, allowing anchor prefixes to reach across lines to a distant '='-adjacent value. 3) In multiline YAML/JSON structures (e.g. 'cfg:
  secret:
    api_key: <cred>
'), the separator \s*(:\s*|=)\s* matches newlines, causing the parent key 'secret:' to match across lines and swallow the nested key 'api_key' as the value, replacing the key name with ******* and leaving the actual credential verbatim and unmasked. The anchor matched the wrong token, which is actively destructive.
goal: Harden redact_text and redaction patterns against key omission, multiline newline bleeding, and nested anchor destruction: 1) WIDEN ACCEPTED KEY PATTERNS: Expand the recognized credential key alternations to include bare 'key' (word-bounded \bkey\b so as not to over-mask benign variables like cache_key or sort_key unless secret-adjacent), 'pwd', 'passwd', 'client_secret', 'db_password', 'credential', 'credentials', and related standard secret identifiers, without degrading retention of diagnostic keys. 2) LINE-SCOPED URL QUERY ANCHORS: Fix the URL-query regex anchor so [^=\r\n]*= replaces [^=]*=, ensuring URL query parameter anchors never cross newline boundaries. 3) LINE-SCOPED KEY/VALUE SEPARATORS: Ensure key-value separators do not cross newlines (e.g. using [ \t]*(:[ \t]*|=)[ \t]* or strictly line-scoped separators), preventing a parent YAML/JSON dictionary key (such as 'secret:') from matching across newlines and swallowing a nested key name (such as 'api_key:') as its value. 4) PRESERVE INVARIANTS & DIAGNOSTIC RETENTION: Maintain high diagnostic retention for non-secret logs, command arguments, and benign variables (e.g. compat, impact, sort_key). Keep all fixtures synthetic (_fake_token) to avoid triggering GitHub push protection. 5) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Add comprehensive hermetic tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py covering all three witness patterns: bare key/pwd/credential masking, multiline URL-query anchor isolation, and multiline YAML/JSON nested key preservation with proper credential redaction. description: Every Holon flow run appends to the same three files -- holon-knowledge/ledger/{intents,plans,executions}.jsonl. When two flows are in flight concurrently or sequentially branched from an older base, git reports merge conflicts on those files. When a PR has merge conflicts against main (mergeable=CONFLICTING, mergeStateStatus=DIRTY), GitHub Actions does not generate the refs/pull/<PR>/merge ref, causing test workflows (Test - Unit, Test - Integration, Test - Hygiene, Run Make) to be skipped entirely without failing. Only jobs running on refs/pull/<PR>/head (such as CodeQL) report status, making the PR appear falsely green while the entire CI test signal was silently dropped. As demonstrated in Bean 0019 (PR #59) and Bean 0062 (PR #64), append-only JSONL files have well-defined union semantics and should never cause unmergeable PRs or dropped CI signals.
goal: Implement robust ledger reconciliation and conflict guards in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py and executor.py so concurrent flow runs never drop the CI signal: 1) AUTOMATIC LEDGER UNION RECONCILIATION: Implement a deterministic ledger merge/union utility (reconcile_ledger_file / reconcile_ledgers) that resolves JSONL conflicts by union: deduplicate rows by canonical primary key ('branch'/'slug' for intents.jsonl, 'plan_id' for plans.jsonl, 'execution_id' for executions.jsonl), preserve all valid JSON rows, and order entries chronologically by 'created_at'. 2) EXECUTOR PRE-PUSH SYNC: In executor.py, before pushing the execution branch to origin, check if origin/main has advanced. If diverged, attempt a merge; if conflicts occur strictly in holon-knowledge/ledger/*.jsonl, automatically resolve them via the union utility, verify that only ledger files were in conflict, stage the resolved ledgers, and commit the merge so the pushed branch is cleanly mergeable. If non-ledger code conflicts occur, abort the auto-merge and fail loudly. 3) FLOW & REVIEW PR MERGEABILITY GUARDS: In flow.py (run_review_stage and PipelineEngine), inspect git/PR mergeability status. Detect when mergeStateStatus is DIRTY or mergeable is CONFLICTING, surface a loud and explicit error/warning that CI tests are suppressed by merge conflicts, and prevent the review stage from falsely declaring consensus approval when CI test workflows did not run on the merge ref. 4) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Add unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_flow.py and test_executor.py covering: ledger union deduplication and chronological ordering, automatic conflict resolution for all 3 ledger files, loud abort on non-ledger conflict, and DIRTY merge state detection.
